bug_semantics: CWE-94 code injection in `aeon/datasets/_tss_data_loaders.py`: `load_time_series_segmentation_benchmark` registered pandas CSV converters for `change_points` and `time_series` as `lambda val: np.array(eval(val))`. Loading a downloaded or locally present attacker-influenced benchmark CSV therefore evaluated a cell as unrestricted Python in the caller's process, yielding arbitrary code execution when the victim invoked the loader. The same original feature commit also used the unsafe pattern in the companion human-activity loader.
flaw_origin: Original feature implementation, not a move or refactor: PR #1755 member commit 849946a6862cf8392c1464eb9b8eb63c9007934f created `aeon/datasets/_tss_data_loaders.py` and first added both the vulnerable loader and the unrestricted `eval(val)` converter. GitHub later squash-landed the two-member PR as 8f81a7324a4f116dd862feda68788b03ff9dc39b.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object for 849946a6862cf8392c1464eb9b8eb63c9007934f identifies author Arik Ermshaus and committer Arik Ermshaus (both non-bot; patch author address `ermshaua@informatik.hu-berlin.de`), has the subject `Added time series segmentation benchmark (TSSB) and human activity segmentation data set loaders + tests.`, an empty body, and no trailers; specifically no AI-bot identity, `Co-authored-by`, `Generated-with`, Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or other AI marker.
evidence: Advisories: GitHub GHSA https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvfj-hqjq-cmgm and NVD https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-18287 identify `load_time_series_segmentation_benchmark`, CWE-94, and user-interaction-dependent arbitrary code execution; reporter detail is https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/advisories/ZDI-26-470/ (ZDI-26-470/ZDI-CAN-29159).

BIC/member evidence: https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/commit/849946a6862cf8392c1464eb9b8eb63c9007934f and its patch https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/commit/849946a6862cf8392c1464eb9b8eb63c9007934f.patch create `aeon/datasets/_tss_data_loaders.py`; added lines 96-102 define the TSSB columns and `converters = {col: lambda val: np.array(eval(val)) for col in np_cols}`, then pass those converters to `pd.read_csv` for both the downloaded ZIP and saved CSV. Added lines 195-227 contain the analogous unrestricted `eval` in the companion loader.

Direct-parent verification: the BIC commit object names parent 800c3b5388219850c853d14201a9e841187851f6. Its datasets tree https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/tree/800c3b5388219850c853d14201a9e841187851f6/aeon/datasets contains no `_tss_data_loaders.py`, and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/800c3b5388219850c853d14201a9e841187851f6/aeon/datasets/_tss_data_loaders.py returns 404; thus the vulnerable file and lines are absent in the immediate parent.

Squash decomposition: PR https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/pull/1755 has two reconstructable member commits. Its patch https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/pull/1755.patch identifies 849946a6862cf8392c1464eb9b8eb63c9007934f as patch 1/2 and 152917bf6c8c3c719e5e01f59ae7c1bc2c625e3f as patch 2/2. The second member only corrects a documentation typo and extends tests (https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/commit/152917bf6c8c3c719e5e01f59ae7c1bc2c625e3f); it does not introduce the sink. The one-parent landing aggregate is https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/commit/8f81a7324a4f116dd862feda68788b03ff9dc39b, so the smaller first member is the causal BIC.

Fix evidence: vendor commit https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/commit/751918052c0cce266b4f7cd4b084408526efc015 directly replaces both `np.array(eval(val))` converter forms in `aeon/datasets/_tss_data_loaders.py` with `_parse_np_array`, imports `ast.literal_eval`, and implements `_parse_np_array` as `np.array(literal_eval(val))` with malformed literals rejected as `ValueError`. This removes general Python evaluation. The same commit also replaces an unrelated `allow_pickle=True` load in `aeon/datasets/_rehabpile_loader.py`; no later indirect commit is needed for the advisory sink.

Affected boundary: tag v0.9.0 predates the feature and has no `aeon/datasets/_tss_data_loaders.py` (tree: https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/tree/v0.9.0/aeon/datasets). The PR member was squash-landed before v0.10.0, and v0.10.0 contains the vulnerable `eval` implementation: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/v0.10.0/aeon/datasets/_tss_data_loaders.py. Therefore v0.10.0 is the first affected release.

Fixed boundary: v1.4.0 still contains both unrestricted `eval` converters (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/v1.4.0/aeon/datasets/_tss_data_loaders.py), while v1.5.0 imports `literal_eval`, routes converters through `_parse_np_array`, and contains no loader `eval` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/v1.5.0/aeon/datasets/_tss_data_loaders.py). Thus the source-verified affected range is v0.10.0 through v1.4.0 and the fixed boundary is v1.5.0; fix 751918052c0cce266b4f7cd4b084408526efc015 is present by the patched tag.

BIC-only attribution evidence: the embedded commit object at https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/commit/849946a6862cf8392c1464eb9b8eb63c9007934f records the same human as author and committer, an empty body, and no trailers. The commit-format patch independently provides `From: Arik Ermshaus <ermshaua@informatik.hu-berlin.de>` and no attribution trailer. No AI inference was drawn from the squash aggregate, PR discussion, fix, or surrounding commits.
reasoning: The vulnerability is the unrestricted evaluation boundary, not merely CSV parsing: pandas invokes the registered converter on attacker-influenced cell text, and the converter passes it directly to Python `eval`, allowing an expression to execute with process privileges. Source-history reconstruction matters because mainline commit 8f81a7324a4f116dd862feda68788b03ff9dc39b is a squash aggregate. PR #1755's preserved two-patch series shows that 849946a6862cf8392c1464eb9b8eb63c9007934f alone created the file and wrote the vulnerable converter; 152917bf6c8c3c719e5e01f59ae7c1bc2c625e3f only changed a citation typo and tests. The BIC's immediate parent 800c3b5388219850c853d14201a9e841187851f6 lacks the entire path, proving direct-parent absence. The mainline landing precedes v0.10.0; tag snapshots prove v0.9.0 lacks the feature, v0.10.0 and v1.4.0 are vulnerable, and v1.5.0 has the literal-only parser from direct fix 751918052c0cce266b4f7cd4b084408526efc015. Finally, BIC-only attribution finds a human author/committer and no AI marker or trailer, so under the required BIC-only rule the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
